From code to Methods

from almkanal import (
    AlmKanal, Filter, Resample,
    preprocessing_report,
)

pipeline = AlmKanal(steps=[
    Filter(highpass=1.0, lowpass=40.0),
    Resample(sfreq=200),
])

# raw: your existing MNE Raw object

pipeline.generate_json("history.json")

Assumes an existing raw object. The quick start includes a complete example with synthetic data.

items.title: AlmKanal
items.text:
Flexible, modular and extendable preprocessing pipelines for M/EEG data

Build and run preprocessing pipelines, keep track of the settings, and generate a Methods draft from your processing history.

Get started → Create your own step

items.title: Offline filtering
items.text: A band-pass filter (1–40 Hz) was applied to the continuous data. The finite impulse response (FIR) filter was designed using firwin with a hamming window. A symmetric linear-phase filter with delay compensation was used, resulting in zero-phase, non-causal filtering. The realized filter length was 661 samples (3.305 s), corresponding to FIR order 660. The lower and upper transition bandwidths were 1.0 Hz and 10.0 Hz, respectively. The −6 dB cutoff frequencies were 0.5 Hz and 45.0 Hz, located at the midpoints of the lower and upper transition bands. Filter design and reporting was aimed to follow recommended practices for electrophysiological data (1, 2).

items.title: Resampling
items.text: The continuous data were resampled from 1000.0 Hz to 200 Hz using FFT-based resampling with a boxcar frequency-domain window.

items.title: References
items.text:
1. Widmann, A., Schröger, E., & Maess, B. (2015). Digital filter design for electrophysiological data: A practical approach. Journal of Neuroscience Methods, 250, 34–46. doi:10.1016/j.jneumeth.2014.08.002

  2. Keil, A., Debener, S., Gratton, G., Junghöfer, M., Kappenman, E. S., Luck, S. J., Luu, P., Miller, G. A., & Yee, C. M. (2014). Committee report: Publication guidelines and recommendations for studies using EEG and MEG. Psychophysiology, 51(1), 1–21. https://doi.org/10.1111/psyp.12147

Disclaimer

AlmKanal renders Methods descriptions from saved processing history and Jinja templates. Review the generated text and describe any earlier processing separately.

items.title: What you can do with AlmKanal
items.text:
AlmKanal builds on MNE-Python by bringing commonly used preprocessing functions together in a modular pipeline framework. Feel free to use the existing steps, add your own, or start with data that have already been processed.

  • Pipelines in Python

    Define and configure processing steps directly in Python. The pipeline makes the order of operations explicit.

    Build a pipeline →

  • Your own processing steps

    Add a custom AlmKanalStep when you need an operation that is not covered by the built-in steps.

    Create your own step →

  • Step-order checks

    Steps can declare which operations must come before or after them. AlmKanal checks those constraints before processing starts.

    Understand validation →

  • A record of what ran

    Save the preprocessing settings used in a pipeline and generate an editable draft of the Methods section from that history.

    Generate Methods text →

  • Use existing MNE data

    Apply compatible steps to MNE Raw or Epochs objects, including recordings that have already been preprocessed.

    Work with existing data →

  • Audio and eye-tracking alignment

    Tools for working with M/EEG recordings alongside WAV audio stimuli and VPixx eye-tracking data.

    Eye tracking → Audio alignment →

items.title: About AlmKanal
items.text:
AlmKanal is developed at the Salzburg Brain Dynamics Lab. It builds on MNE-Python and brings together explicit Python pipelines, user-defined processing steps, supported ordering checks, multimodal alignment, and Methods reporting.

Its pipeline architecture is inspired by scikit-learn's make_pipeline API. Text configuration files remain useful in other workflows; AlmKanal emphasizes direct composition in Python.

items.title: AlmKanal
items.text:
from almkanal import AlmKanal

pipeline = AlmKanal(steps, pick_params=None)

steps is an ordered list of AlmKanalStep objects. Construction checks their declared ordering and repetition rules. pick_params, when provided, controls channel-type selection before processing.

items.title: run
items.text:
processed, report = pipeline.run(data)

Runs steps sequentially and returns the final step's data output and an mne.Report. Inputs may be Raw, Epochs, or homogeneous lists, subject to step compatibility.

The processing history is reset at the start of each run. The callable shorthand pipeline(data) also delegates to run() and returns its pair of outputs.

items.title: generate_json
items.text:
pipeline.generate_json(path='/my/path/to/file.json', max_elements=50)

Builds a JSON-compatible history dictionary; optionally writes it to path. Call it after a successful run. max_elements limits sequence serialization and can omit large contents from the compact record. Create the destination directory before writing a file there.

items.title: info
items.text:
pipeline.info contains the recorded step history and context. For durable reporting, save a JSON history for each run rather than relying on mutable in-memory state using: 

pipeline.generate_json(path='/my/path/to/file.json', max_elements=50)

items.title: AlmKanalStep
items.text:
from almkanal import AlmKanalStep

Subclass the base AlmKanalStep class and implement run(data, info) and reports(data, report, info). The first returns a dictionary with a "data" entry plus metadata; the second receives the processed data and updated context and may add report content.

Use must_be_before, must_be_after, and allow_repeated for supported construction-time checks. See validation for their exact scope.

items.title: Defaults API
items.text:
set_defaults(profile="generic", **sections) selects general defaults, the "salzburg" profile, or a Defaults object and applies optional section overrides. It returns the activated profile. Each call starts from the selected profile; pass get_defaults() to extend the active settings. use_defaults() accepts the same arguments within a temporary with block.

Defaults.generic() and Defaults.salzburg() construct reusable profiles; profile.with_overrides(...) returns a customized copy. configure(profile) activates an already-built profile. See Defaults and lab profiles for available sections, capture timing, and examples.

items.title: Further documentation
items.text:
For detailed documentation of individual classes and parameters, see the automatically generated API reference for AlmKanal, AlmKanalStep, and the preprocessing steps. The API reference is generated directly from the Python docstrings.

For practical examples, see VPixx alignment, WAV alignment, and Methods reporting.

items.title: Methods reporting
items.text: AlmKanal can automatically generate draft Methods text from the processing history saved after running a pipeline. The public interface for this is preprocessing_report, which uses Jinja templates to describe the preprocessing steps.

items.title: Example
items.text:
After running a pipeline and saving its processing history:

from almkanal import preprocessing_report

pipeline.generate_json("history.json")

methods_path = preprocessing_report(
    files=["history.json"],
    out_path="methods.md",
)

The example writes the generated text to methods.md. Other output formats, such as Word documents or PDFs, require Pandoc (and, for PDF, a suitable PDF engine).

items.title: Custom Jinja templates
items.text:
You can also use your own Jinja templates to customize the generated descriptions:

methods_path = preprocessing_report(
    files=["history.json"],
    out_path="methods.md",
    template_dir="my_templates",
)

See Custom Methods templates for instructions on creating and using your own templates.

Note

Automatically generated Methods text should always be reviewed before use in a publication. Processing performed before the data entered AlmKanal needs to be documented separately.

items.title: Define trials and their WAV files
items.text:
StimulusSpanSpec describes raw-sample trial spans and their corresponding stimuli. EpochStimuls uses a function that creates this specification from the input recording, prepares WAV features, and returns fixed-length epochs.

The following is an acquisition-dependent example. It assumes known onset/end trigger codes and a recorded-audio channel. Replace those values with your experiment's mapping.

from pathlib import Path

import mne
from almkanal import AlmKanal, EpochStimuls, StimulusSpanSpec

AUDIO_DIR = Path("stimuli")

def make_spans(raw):
    return StimulusSpanSpec.from_events(
        raw,
        onset_trigger_to_wav={1: "story.wav"},
        end_triggers=[2],
        stim_channel="STI101",
        base_audio_path=AUDIO_DIR,
    )

raw = mne.io.read_raw_fif("your_recording_raw.fif", preload=True)
pipeline = AlmKanal([
    EpochStimuls(
        gen_span_spec=make_spans,
        base_audio_path=AUDIO_DIR,
        audio_channels=["AUDIO"],  # Your actual recorded-audio channel.
        feature=["envelope", "pitch_voicing"],
        resample_sfreq=200.0,
        epoch_len_s=5.0,
        hw_delay_s=0.0,  # Only when the reference represents sound at the ears.
        on_alignment_error="raise",
    ),
])

epochs, qc_report = pipeline.run(raw.copy())
pipeline.generate_json("audio_preprocessing.json")

This prepares data for downstream analysis. It does not, by itself, fit a TRF model or compute coherence.

items.title: Distinguish three alignment modes
items.text:
Configuration What happens Recorded audio_channels supplied Offset and clock drift are estimated from recorded audio and the WAV No audio channels, realign_without_audio=True Alignment uses WAV duration and an assumed drift; onset is assumed, not measured No audio channels, realign_without_audio=False No clock realignment is performed; trial timing and any physical-delay correction are used

Do not describe an assumed-drift correction as an empirical synchronization estimate. Recorded audio takes precedence when supplied; failed audio fits do not silently fall back to assumed drift.

items.title: Measure physical delays for your setup
items.text:
Clock alignment and hardware-delay correction solve different problems. hw_delay_s is applied after realignment. Positive values advance neural events relative to the WAV features; the feature channels are not shifted.

The package's default delay and fallback drift reflect particular assumptions. They are not universal constants. Use a measured delay for your acquisition system, or zero when your recorded reference already represents sound arrival at the ears.

items.title: Inspect alignment diagnostics
items.text:
Review the QC output and recorded metadata for offset, drift, residual error, correspondence strength, rejected or skipped trials, and retained epochs. Long stimuli can need a wider alignment search interval to accommodate accumulated clock drift.

Quality warnings can be emitted even when an alignment is applied. on_alignment_error="raise" stops actual failures; it is not an automatic rejection rule for every questionable fit. Use study-specific acceptance criteria and keep them with the analysis.

Preserve trigger and recorded-audio channels until they have been used, and avoid preprocessing away the bandwidth needed for alignment.

items.title: Choose the sampling frequency and audio features
items.text:
resample_sfreq sets the output sampling frequency in Hz. With None, the input sampling frequency is retained. Trial spans and trigger samples always refer to the original recording. Alignment and the sample-rounded physical-delay correction run at that original rate. Each continuous trial segment is then resampled before audio features are computed at the output rate and appended. This preserves the available recorded-audio bandwidth for alignment and avoids resampling already appended features. An earlier resampling step reduces the bandwidth available to alignment.

Segment resampling uses MNE's FFT method with a boxcar frequency-domain window, automatic padding, and reflect_limited edge padding. MNE applies anti-aliasing internally. Annotations are preserved when preserve_annotations=True; epochs overlapping bad annotations are rejected. Reports record the original and output sampling frequencies, resampling method, and processing order.

feature accepts either one feature name or a nonempty sequence of distinct feature names. Channels are appended in the requested feature order as misc channels. Single-channel features use the requested feature name. Multichannel features use that name followed by component or band identifiers:

Feature Appended channels envelope envelope (RMS amplitude) rectify rectify_pos_rect, rectify_neg_rect mel mel_1_<frequency>Hz, … flux flux (onset strength) mel_onsets mel_onsets_1_<frequency>Hz, … pitch pitch (fundamental frequency in Hz) pitch_voicing pitch_voicing_log2_f0_centered, pitch_voicing_voicing

Mel band indices start at one and frequency labels are rounded band centers. Feature names must not repeat, and appended channel names must not overlap recording channels. audio_cutoff_hz controls the feature low-pass filter; feature extraction details are described by prepare_audio. Features share the output sampling grid; only the common recording/feature duration contributes epochs, and incomplete trailing epochs are discarded.

The standalone build_stimulus_epochs helper accepts the same feature and resample_sfreq parameters with an existing StimulusSpanSpec.

items.title: Share stimulus-processing defaults
items.text:
Use the stimuli defaults section to configure shared settings for EpochStimuls, build_stimulus_epochs, trial-end inference, and assumed drift:

from almkanal import Defaults, set_defaults

profile = Defaults.generic().with_overrides(
    stimuli={
        "resample_sfreq": 200.0,
        "feature": ["envelope", "pitch_voicing"],
        "epoch_len_s": 5.0,
    },
)
set_defaults(profile)

# Inspect a detached copy of the stimulus settings.
settings = profile.stimuli

Explicit step or helper arguments take precedence over profile settings. Each step captures its profile when constructed; changing the active defaults later does not change an existing step's configuration.

items.title: Match three names
items.text:
A custom reporting extension connects the step class name, the registered StepSpec, and the Jinja partial filename. This example continues the NotchAtFrequency tutorial.

NotchAtFrequency
    -> StepSpec registered as "NotchAtFrequency"
    -> templates/steps/NotchAtFrequency.j2

The example's metadata contains one nested notch_info dictionary, so the context builder extracts it before applying the specification.

items.title: Register a specification
items.text:
Run this registration in the same Python process as your Methods export:

from almkanal.report.stepspecs import StepSpec, keys_selector, register

register(
    "NotchAtFrequency",
    StepSpec(settings_fn=keys_selector("frequency_hz")),
)

settings_fn selects settings that must match across histories. A summarize_fn can separately summarize per-recording results. Do not discard meaningful protocol differences just to pass a consistency check.

For a reusable extension, put registration code in an importable module or package. The reporting API's step_packages argument can load it alongside the built-in specifications.

items.title: Add the prose template
items.text:
Create my_templates/steps/NotchAtFrequency.j2:

A notch filter was applied to the continuous recordings at
{{ s.settings.frequency_hz }} Hz using MNE-Python.

The packaged master template passes each step context as s. Its settings and summarized results are accessible as s.settings and s.results. The filename is case-sensitive.

This is intentionally minimal wording for a minimal teaching step. Before publication, extend the step metadata and prose to include the filter characteristics, relevant citations, and other details needed to reproduce the operation.

items.title: Render with your override
items.text:
from almkanal import preprocessing_report

preprocessing_report(
    files=["preprocessing.json"],
    out_path="methods.md",
    template_dir="my_templates",
)

Your directory is checked first. Packaged templates remain available for other steps. Steps without a named partial use the packaged fallback template; that fallback is not a substitute for a carefully written scientific description.

items.title: Catch missing information
items.text:
The renderer uses Jinja's StrictUndefined. Referring to metadata that does not exist should therefore fail rather than quietly producing a blank value. Test both a valid history and one with a missing required setting.

A custom master template can be selected with master_template. Inspect the packaged master before replacing it, especially when retaining step ordering and references.

The examples page includes a registration script and template directory that can be copied together.

items.title: The step contract
items.text:
A step subclasses AlmKanalStep and implements two methods. run(data, info) returns a dictionary containing at least "data". Other entries become processing metadata. reports(data, report, info) adds diagnostics to the MNE report after execution.

The info object carries pipeline context. Returning metadata is the route for recording a step's results; changing the copy passed to run() is not a way to update the pipeline's shared history.

items.title: A continuous-data notch filter
items.text:
This teaching example wraps MNE's notch filter. It intentionally accepts only Raw data and records the requested frequency. It is not a complete publication-grade record of every filter parameter.

import mne
from attrs import define, field
from almkanal import AlmKanalStep

@define
class NotchAtFrequency(AlmKanalStep):
    frequency: float = 50.0
    must_be_before: tuple[str, ...] = field(
        default=("SourceReconstruction",), init=False
    )

    def run(self, data, info):
        if not isinstance(data, mne.io.BaseRaw):
            raise TypeError("NotchAtFrequency requires continuous Raw data.")
        if not 0 < self.frequency < data.info["sfreq"] / 2:
            raise ValueError("Frequency must be between zero and Nyquist.")
        data.load_data().notch_filter(freqs=[self.frequency])
        return {
            "data": data,
            "notch_info": {"frequency_hz": self.frequency},
        }

    def reports(self, data, report, info):
        report.add_raw(
            data,
            title="After notch filtering",
            butterfly=False,
            psd=True,
        )

The must_be_before declaration makes the step participate in supported ordering checks. To make an epoched-data version, implement and test an operation appropriate to that data structure rather than simply removing the type check.

items.title: Compose it with built-in steps
items.text:
from almkanal import AlmKanal, Filter, Resample

pipeline = AlmKanal([
    NotchAtFrequency(frequency=50.0),
    Filter(highpass=1.0, lowpass=40.0),
    Resample(sfreq=200),
])

# raw is your loaded continuous recording.
processed, report = pipeline.run(raw.copy())
pipeline.generate_json("preprocessing.json")

Choose filtering settings for your data. The sequence demonstrates composition; it is not a recommendation that this combination is necessary for every study.

items.title: Record what matters
items.text: Prefer explicit, JSON-friendly metadata with named units. Distinguish chosen settings from data-dependent results. For a production filter step, also capture its design, bandwidth, effective length, and other scientifically relevant settings. Do not assume that the constructor's parameters are automatically recorded: include relevant values in the result returned by run().

items.title: Add Methods support
items.text: Custom-step execution and custom scientific prose are separate extension points. See custom Methods templates for a StepSpec and Jinja partial matching NotchAtFrequency.

items.title: Test the contract
items.text:
Test valid and invalid inputs, ordering errors, output shape and units, metadata, and report generation. Tests should establish that invalid data fails clearly and that important settings appear in the history and rendered description.

The downloadable custom-step example contains this implementation with type annotations.

items.title: Defaults for your lab or study
items.text: AlmKanal lets you choose shared defaults for your whole lab or for a particular study. Values you supply in individual function calls still take precedence.

items.title: Use a lab profile
items.text:
To use the built-in Salzburg settings, add this near the beginning of your script:

import almkanal as ak

ak.set_defaults("salzburg")

Then build your pipeline as usual:

pipeline = ak.AlmKanal(
    steps=[
        ak.Filter(),
        ak.Resample(sfreq=200),
    ]
)

The steps use the selected defaults for any optional arguments you leave out. Once you have loaded your MNE recording as raw, run the pipeline with processed_raw, report = pipeline.run(raw).

If you do not select a profile, AlmKanal uses general defaults automatically. Calling ak.set_defaults() resets the active settings to those general defaults.

items.title: Adjust settings for a study
items.text:
You can start from a lab profile and change just the settings needed for a study:

ak.set_defaults("salzburg", filter={"lowpass": 30.0})

step = ak.Filter()              # Uses the study's 30 Hz low-pass setting.
custom = ak.Filter(lowpass=20)  # Uses 20 Hz for this step only.

Options are grouped into sections such as filter, ica, stimuli, and vpixx. Unspecified options retain their values from the selected profile. The complete list of sections, types, and general defaults is at the end of this guide.

items.title: Create and save your own lab profile
items.text:
Another lab can define a reusable profile using Defaults.generic() as a starting point. Save the following in a file called lab_defaults.py, alongside your analysis scripts:

# lab_defaults.py
from almkanal import Defaults

LAB_DEFAULTS = Defaults.generic().with_overrides(
    name="our-lab",
    version="1",
    filter={"highpass": 0.5, "lowpass": 40.0},
    events={"stim_channel": "TRIGGER"},
)

Replace these example values with your lab's settings. with_overrides() creates a new profile and leaves the original unchanged. Defining a profile does not activate it.

items.title: Load and use the saved profile
items.text:
Import the profile in any analysis script and activate it with set_defaults():

import almkanal as ak
from lab_defaults import LAB_DEFAULTS

ak.set_defaults(LAB_DEFAULTS)

pipeline = ak.AlmKanal(
    steps=[
        ak.Filter(),
        ak.Resample(sfreq=200),
    ]
)

Importing lab_defaults.py recreates the profile from the saved values. To share it across projects, put the module in a shared Python package that your scripts can import. Keeping this file under version control also records changes to your lab's settings. Update its version when changing an agreed configuration.

The profile's name is a label for processing records; it does not register a new string shortcut. Use ak.set_defaults(LAB_DEFAULTS) to load your own profile. The built-in string shortcuts are "generic" and "salzburg".

Profiles are saved here as ordinary Python files. Built-in loaders for JSON, YAML, or TOML profile files are not currently available.

items.title: Derive a study profile from your lab profile
items.text:
A study can reuse the lab settings while overriding a few values:

# study_defaults.py
from lab_defaults import LAB_DEFAULTS

STUDY_DEFAULTS = LAB_DEFAULTS.with_overrides(
    name="auditory-study",
    version="1",
    filter={"lowpass": 30.0},
)

The lab profile stays unchanged. Save this definition in study_defaults.py, then load it in your analysis script:

import almkanal as ak
from study_defaults import STUDY_DEFAULTS

ak.set_defaults(STUDY_DEFAULTS)

items.title: General and Salzburg settings
items.text:
The Salzburg profile starts from the general defaults and changes these values:

Setting General profile Salzburg profile ica.train False True stimuli.hw_delay_s 0.0 seconds 0.0165 seconds stimuli.fallback_drift_us_per_s 0.0 µs/s 499.0 µs/s stimuli.audio_channels None ("MISC007", "MISC008") vpixx.meg_stim_channel None (MNE detection) "STI101" vpixx.meg_min_duration 0.0 seconds 0.002 seconds vpixx.meg_max_trigger None (keep all codes) 4096 (exclude this code and above) vpixx.screen_distance Must be configured for radians 0.82 m vpixx.screen_size Must be configured for radians (0.61, 0.34) m vpixx.screen_resolution Must be configured for radians (1920, 1080) pixels ica_eog.left_eog_chs Must be configured when using the helper ["MEG0121", "MEG0311"] ica_eog.right_eog_chs Must be configured when using the helper ["MEG1211", "MEG1411"]

For another setup, supply its measured geometry, timing values, and channel names. Selecting a profile does not check whether its hardware settings match your recording.

Salzburg's audio channels enable recorded-audio alignment during stimulus processing. If a recording has no audio channels, use ak.set_defaults("salzburg", stimuli={"audio_channels": None}) or pass audio_channels=None to the individual EpochStimuls step.

items.title: When settings take effect
items.text:
Set defaults before constructing your steps. Existing steps keep the values and profile they captured when they were created:

ak.set_defaults("generic", filter={"lowpass": 30.0})
first = ak.Filter()

ak.set_defaults("generic", filter={"lowpass": 40.0})
second = ak.Filter()

print(first.lowpass)   # 30.0
print(second.lowpass)  # 40.0

Built-in steps also run their internal helpers and callbacks under their captured profile. Standalone functions resolve omitted arguments when called.

Explicit arguments always win, including None, False, and 0 where those values are supported:

ak.set_defaults("salzburg")

unfiltered_lowpass = ak.Filter(lowpass=None)
without_train_removal = ak.ICA(train=False)

Required inputs remain required. For example, Resample still needs sfreq, ForwardModel needs subject_id and subjects_dir, and EpochStimuls needs its span callback and audio path. Profiles do not replace the pipeline's step ordering requirements.

items.title: Repeated calls and validation
items.text:
Each set_defaults() call starts from the selected profile, which is "generic" when omitted. It does not accumulate earlier customizations. To extend your active settings explicitly, pass get_defaults():

ak.set_defaults("salzburg", filter={"lowpass": 30.0})
ak.set_defaults(ak.get_defaults(), ica={"random_state": 123})

This keeps the 30 Hz low-pass setting and changes the ICA random seed. set_defaults() returns the activated profile if you want to keep it in a variable.

Unknown sections or options and incompatible value types raise an error before the active defaults change. Processing functions still check scientific constraints, such as whether a cutoff suits the recording's sampling rate.

A dictionary supplied as an option replaces that whole option; dictionaries are not recursively merged. For example, supply a complete IIR configuration:

ak.set_defaults(
    LAB_DEFAULTS,
    filter={"method": "iir", "iir_params": {"order": 4, "ftype": "butter"}},
)

The lower-level configure(profile) activates an already-built Defaults object. For most scripts, set_defaults() is sufficient.

items.title: VPixx eye tracking
items.text:
VPixxCleaner and the standalone eye-tracking helpers share the vpixx section. Sampling rate comes from the recording's timestamps. Screen size and viewing distance are in metres; resolution is in pixels:

ak.set_defaults(
    LAB_DEFAULTS,
    vpixx={
        "screen_resolution": (1920, 1080),
        "screen_size": (0.53, 0.30),
        "screen_distance": 0.65,
        "meg_stim_channel": "TRIGGER",
    },
)

step = ak.VPixxCleaner(eye_path="eye.mat", interpolate_blinks=False)

Replace the example geometry with your equipment's values. The general profile requires these three geometry settings for conversion to radians. Pixel-only processing with convert_to_radians=False does not require geometry.

eye_path remains required. Set concatenate_raws=True to combine a list of recording blocks after cleaning; a single recording returns a single Raw object. The align option controls only the standalone add_eye_tracking_data() helper; VPixxCleaner always aligns eye tracking to its input recordings.

VPixxConfig() captures its omitted values at construction. The standalone load_eyetracking_data(), add_eye_tracking_data(), and align_eye_to_meg() resolve omitted options at call time. An omitted or None config builds a fresh VPixxConfig from the active profile. An explicit config supplies its own geometry and calibration settings; other loading and alignment arguments still use the active profile unless explicitly supplied.

vpixx.blink_buffer_vpixx supplies VPixxConfig.blink_buffer. vpixx.blink_buffer overrides that buffer during loading; None uses the config's buffer and (0.0, 0.0) uses no padding. Explicit None also overrides a profile's non-None loading buffer.

meg_max_trigger=None retains all trigger codes. meg_stim_channel=None uses MNE's stimulus-channel detection.

items.title: Temporary settings
items.text:
For a temporary comparison, use_defaults() accepts the same profile and section overrides as set_defaults():

ak.set_defaults("salzburg")

with ak.use_defaults("generic", filter={"lowpass": 25.0}):
    comparison_filter = ak.Filter()

# Salzburg is active again; comparison_filter keeps its 25 Hz setting.

Blocks can be nested. The previous profile is restored even if an exception leaves the block. Steps created inside can be run afterward.

items.title: Inspect and record settings
items.text:
profile = ak.get_defaults()

print(profile.name)
print(profile.filter.lowpass)
filter_settings = profile.section("filter")
all_settings = profile.to_dict()

Profiles protect their values from accidental changes. Section objects and returned dictionaries are independent copies; editing them does not change the active profile. Use with_overrides() or set_defaults() to customize it.

After a pipeline runs, each built-in step records its profile name, version, and resolved configurable parameters, including explicit overrides. Save the processing history with:

pipeline.generate_json("preprocessing.json")

The JSON contains an ordered processing_history list, with separate settings for each occurrence of a step. It is a processing record, not a loadable lab profile. Keep your profile's Python file alongside the analysis, particularly when callbacks also use helper defaults.

items.title: Concurrent execution
items.text: Active settings are local to the current execution context. Async tasks inherit the context in which they are created; later changes remain local to each task. Configure worker threads and processes explicitly, or pass an appropriate context or already-constructed steps. Setting a profile in one process does not configure every worker.

items.title: Synthetic-data quick start
items.text:
Download quickstart.py. It creates a reproducible synthetic EEG recording, runs filtering and resampling, saves the processed data and QC report, and renders Markdown Methods text.

python quickstart.py

No study-data download is needed. The script creates almkanal-demo/ in the current directory.

items.title: Constructor validation
items.text:
Download validation_demo.py. It intentionally builds an invalid step sequence and checks that construction raises an error. No M/EEG recording is needed.

python validation_demo.py

items.title: A custom processing and reporting extension
items.text:
Download the complete example bundle for the custom-step workflow. It contains notch_step.py, custom_methods.py, the quick-start helper, and a matching template directory. Extract the files together, then run:

python custom_methods.py

The script runs the teaching notch-filter step with built-in steps, registers its reporting specification, and writes an overridden Methods description. Expand the metadata and template before using a custom scientific procedure in a publication.

items.title: Your own recordings
items.text: The eye-tracking and audio guides use filenames, trigger codes, and calibration values that must be replaced with study-specific inputs. They are not bundled as plug-and-play tests because representative VPixx and recorded-audio files are not part of this documentation package.

items.title: Validation status
items.text: The documentation build checks Python syntax for complete example scripts. Their APIs were cross-checked against the public source, but these AlmKanal examples were not executed end to end in the site-authoring environment. Run them against your installed package revision before adopting them or publishing example outputs. The bundle includes a separate optional example-check command for that purpose.

items.title: Prepare your inputs
items.text:
VPixxCleaner loads eye-tracking data, applies supported cleaning options, aligns it to a continuous recording using the configured trigger channels, and adds eye-tracking channels to the recording.

You need a supported eye-tracking file for each raw recording, identifiable synchronization events, and the correct screen and calibration settings. The guide below is an API example, not a validated recipe for every VPixx export format or acquisition setup.

items.title: Configure the step
items.text:
VPixxCleaner uses the active vpixx defaults profile. The generic profile leaves screen geometry unset; supply it as below, or call set_defaults("salzburg") before creating the step to use the Salzburg setup. Screen dimensions and viewing distance are in metres. Pixel-only processing with convert_to_radians=False does not require screen geometry.

import mne
from almkanal import AlmKanal, VPixxCleaner

raw = mne.io.read_raw_fif("your_recording_raw.fif", preload=True)

pipeline = AlmKanal([
    VPixxCleaner(
        eye_path="path/to/your_supported_vpixx_file",
        meg_stim_channel="STI101",       # Use your actual trigger channel.
        eye_stim_channel="Digital Output",
        screen_resolution=(1920, 1080), # Example setup: replace as needed.
        screen_size=(0.61, 0.34),       # Screen dimensions in metres.
        screen_distance=0.82,          # Viewing distance in metres.
        calibration_eye="right",
        interpolate_blinks=True,
        convert_to_radians=True,
    ),
])

aligned_raw, report = pipeline.run(raw.copy())
pipeline.generate_json("eye_preprocessing.json")

Keep the synchronization channels available until alignment has completed. The example's channel names and dimensions must be replaced when your setup differs.

To reuse settings across scripts and standalone helpers:

from almkanal import set_defaults, VPixxCleaner
from almkanal.eye_utils.gaze_utils import load_eyetracking_data

set_defaults("salzburg", vpixx={"blink_buffer_vpixx": (0.05, 0.25)})
step = VPixxCleaner("eye.mat")
eye = load_eyetracking_data("eye.mat")

The step captures settings at construction; the standalone loader reads the active profile at call time. Explicit arguments override profile values. The loader obtains its sampling rate from the MAT-file timestamps.

items.title: Check the result
items.text: Check event correspondences and timing across the recording, channel names and units, blink handling, and retained samples. The implementation checks equal sampling rates and sample counts before adding eye channels. Matching dimensions alone are not evidence of correct synchronization.

items.title: Work with recording blocks
items.text: For several raw blocks, supply an equally long list of eye-tracking paths. Set concatenate_raws=True only when concatenation is wanted; otherwise the step returns a list and subsequent steps must support it. This is important when you want to do MultiBlockMaxwell afterwards. If you are not using MEG data you probably want to concatenate_raws=True to avoid errors with subsequent steps. Currently only VPIXXCleaner and MultiBlockMaxwell accept lists of Raw or Epoch objects.

items.title: Respect ordering requirements
items.text:
When present together, VPixxCleaner is declared to run before MultiBlockMaxwell, Maxwell, Epochs, and Events. This step requires continuous data; it is not a way to align eye-tracking files to an arbitrary pre-existing Epochs object.

Review the loader and alignment implementation for file-format details and acquisition assumptions before using it on a new recording system.

items.title: Install from GitHub
items.text:
Use Python 3.11 or newer and an environment dedicated to your project. The repository documents installation directly from GitHub:

python -m venv .venv
# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/schmidtfa/AlmKanal.git"

Git must be installed and available on your command line. Package dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml; allow the installer to resolve them rather than installing a hand-written list of scientific packages.

items.title: Check the installation
items.text:
python -c "import almkanal; print(almkanal.__version__)"

Then try the synthetic-data quick start. It needs no downloaded study data, MRI, eye tracker, or audio files.

items.title: Use Pixi
items.text:
For an existing pixi.toml, add the dependency to its pypi-dependencies table:

[pypi-dependencies]
almkanal = { git = "https://github.com/schmidtfa/AlmKanal.git" }

When using pyproject.toml as your Pixi manifest, use [tool.pixi.pypi-dependencies] instead. The AlmKanal repository itself includes a Pixi environment and development tasks.

items.title: Keep a reproducible environment
items.text:
For a study, record the exact software revision and preserve your environment lockfile. A Git dependency can be pinned to a commit rather than following main. Save that identifier with your analysis scripts and outputs.

# Replace COMMIT_SHA with the commit used in your study.
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/schmidtfa/AlmKanal.git@COMMIT_SHA"

items.title: Optional report conversion
items.text:
Markdown Methods output does not require Pandoc. Converting Methods text to other supported formats requires the Pandoc executable on your PATH, or an explicit pandoc_path argument. Installing a Python package named pandoc alone is not a check that the executable is available.

pandoc --version

PDF conversion additionally needs an appropriate PDF engine. See report formats. Source reconstruction and acquisition-specific workflows may need separate anatomical data, system files, or hardware metadata; the quick start does not.

items.title: From execution to scientific prose
items.text:
AlmKanal records processing information as steps run. Export that history to JSON and pass it to the Methods renderer. Jinja templates supply the prose; the saved settings supply the values. This is template-based reporting, not an AI service invoked at runtime.

from almkanal import preprocessing_report

# Run your configured pipeline first.
processed, qc_report = pipeline.run(raw.copy())
pipeline.generate_json("sub-01_preprocessing.json")

preprocessing_report(
    files=["sub-01_preprocessing.json"],
    out_path="methods.md",
)

The quick start provides a complete example, including the input data.

items.title: Three outputs, three purposes
items.text:
Output Purpose MNE HTML report returned by run() Visual and tabular quality control supplied by the steps JSON from generate_json() Recorded processing information for a completed run Text from preprocessing_report() A template-rendered draft of the Methods description

An HTML Methods export is not the same thing as the MNE HTML QC report. Retain both when they serve your workflow.

items.title: Combine compatible histories
items.text:
from pathlib import Path
from almkanal import preprocessing_report

files = sorted(Path("histories").glob("*_preprocessing.json"))
if not files:
    raise FileNotFoundError("No preprocessing histories found.")

preprocessing_report(files=files, out_path="study_methods.md")

The context builder checks that input files share an ordered sequence of steps and matching settings selected by each step's specification. Result summaries are handled separately. Settings mismatches raise errors rather than silently merging distinct protocols.

The context's n_subjects value counts input files. Do not assume this equals participants when several runs or sessions belong to each person. Group and describe your data accordingly.

items.title: Choose an output format
items.text:
The output suffix normally determines the target format; to= can override it.

# Markdown: no Pandoc executable required.
preprocessing_report(files=files, out_path="methods.md")

# These conversions require the Pandoc executable.
preprocessing_report(files=files, out_path="methods.html", to="html")
preprocessing_report(files=files, out_path="methods.docx", to="docx")

PDF additionally requires a PDF engine configured for Pandoc. metadata, extra_args, and pandoc_path allow conversion-specific settings. See the reporting API for the signature.

items.title: Customize the wording
items.text: Pass template_dir to override templates while retaining packaged defaults for other steps. Custom scientific operations should have a matching metadata specification and Methods template. The custom-reporting guide walks through this using the custom notch-filter step.

items.title: Before using the text
items.text:
Review the generated description against your code and outputs. Include preprocessing that happened outside AlmKanal, justify study-specific decisions, check citations, and describe any excluded participants or trials. Verify that custom steps produced meaningful prose rather than only a generic fallback.

The generator helps keep code and documentation close together. It does not certify a Methods section as complete or publication-ready.

items.title: Start from Raw or Epochs
items.text:
AlmKanal accepts MNE continuous and epoched data. A valid input object need not represent an untouched acquisition. For example, ICA or other cleaning may already have been performed outside AlmKanal.

A step still needs to support its input. Continuous-only operations do not become valid on epochs merely because the pipeline accepts both representations.

# Continue an existing analysis; raw is an MNE Raw object.
from almkanal import AlmKanal, Filter, Resample

pipeline = AlmKanal([
    Filter(highpass=1.0, lowpass=40.0),
    Resample(sfreq=200),
])
processed, report = pipeline.run(raw.copy())

items.title: Continue from epoched data
items.text:
For epochs already low-pass filtered to 40 Hz and sampled above 200 Hz, a resampling-only pipeline can be appropriate:

from almkanal import AlmKanal, Resample

# epochs already exists and has been low-pass filtered appropriately.
pipeline = AlmKanal([Resample(sfreq=200)])
processed_epochs, report = pipeline.run(epochs.copy())

This example does not infer or repeat earlier processing. Keep a record of those earlier steps alongside the new history. Confirm the low-pass metadata and input sampling rate before running it.

items.title: Choose channels deliberately
items.text:
pick_params forwards channel-type selection settings to mne.pick_types before the steps execute:

pipeline = AlmKanal(
    steps=[Filter(highpass=1.0, lowpass=40.0)],
    pick_params={"eeg": True, "meg": False, "stim": False},
)

Do not discard trigger, eye-tracking, auxiliary, or recorded-audio channels before a step that needs them. For multimodal pipelines, it may be preferable to select channels within individual steps.

items.title: Protect inputs and preserve history
items.text:
Many operations act in place. Pass a copy when you need the original object later. Save the history after each completed run: the next call to run() clears the pipeline's earlier processing history. Save separate JSON files for separate recordings rather than treating one pipeline instance as a permanent audit log.

The JSON history is a compact processing record, not a replacement for raw data, full numerical results, environment files, or versioned analysis code. Its max_elements setting can limit saved sequence content.

items.title: Multiple recording blocks
items.text: The pipeline also accepts homogeneous lists of Raw objects or homogeneous lists of Epochs objects. Not all steps handle lists. For example, MultiBlockMaxwell handles multiple raw MEG blocks and concatenates them after filtering. Use a list-aware first step and verify the representation it returns before adding ordinary single-recording steps.

items.title: What validation does not do
items.text: AlmKanal cannot reconstruct undocumented preprocessing from your input object, prove that an analysis suits your hypothesis, or validate constraints a custom step never declared. Its role is to make the pipeline explicit and check supported rules, not to choose a study's preprocessing strategy.

items.title: Create a small recording
items.text:
This tutorial uses synthetic EEG to demonstrate the API. Its parameters are examples, not a recommended preprocessing protocol. Install AlmKanal first, then run the following blocks in one Python session.

from pathlib import Path

import mne
import numpy as np
from almkanal import AlmKanal, Filter, Resample, preprocessing_report

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
sfreq = 500.0
times = np.arange(int(30 * sfreq)) / sfreq
signal = 2e-6 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 10 * times)
data = signal[None, :] + rng.normal(0, 1e-6, (4, len(times)))
info = mne.create_info(["Fz", "Cz", "Pz", "Oz"], sfreq, "eeg")
raw = mne.io.RawArray(data, info)
raw.set_montage("standard_1020")

out = Path("almkanal-demo")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

items.title: Define the steps in order
items.text:
pipeline = AlmKanal(
    steps=[
        Filter(highpass=1.0, lowpass=40.0),
        Resample(sfreq=200),
    ]
)

The list is the processing order. Here, explicit low-pass filtering precedes downsampling. Constructing the pipeline checks constraints declared by its steps; data-dependent checks happen when the steps run.

items.title: Run and inspect
items.text:
processed, qc_report = pipeline.run(raw.copy())

qc_report.save(
    out / "quality-control.html",
    overwrite=True,
    open_browser=False,
)
processed.save(out / "processed_raw.fif", overwrite=True)

run() returns two objects: the output of the final step and an MNE report. raw.copy() protects the original recording from steps that modify data in place. The output in this example remains continuous data.

Open the QC report and check the results. Completion without an exception is not a scientific quality check.

items.title: Generate Methods text
items.text:
history_path = out / "preprocessing.json"
pipeline.generate_json(str(history_path))

methods_path = preprocessing_report(
    files=[history_path],
    out_path=out / "methods.md",
)
print(methods_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

The Methods exporter reads the saved history and renders Jinja templates. It does not ask an AI model to describe your recording.

Output What to use it for processed_raw.fif Continue your analysis quality-control.html Inspect processing diagnostics preprocessing.json Retain the recorded processing history methods.md Review and edit draft Methods text

Review the text. Describe earlier processing separately, check scientific terminology and settings, and add study-specific details before using the output in a manuscript.

items.title: Use your own recording
items.text:
Replace the synthetic-data block with the appropriate MNE reader. For example:

raw = mne.io.read_raw_fif("your_recording_raw.fif", preload=True)

Reconsider the channel types, filtering, sampling rate, and artifact handling for your study. See working with your data and the step catalogue.

The complete script is available on the examples page.

items.title: Step catalogue
items.text:
These names are exported by the inspected almkanal package. This catalogue is a navigation guide, not a recommendation to apply every operation.

items.title: Use the right input
items.text:
Filter and Resample target continuous or epoched data. Maxwell filtering, event detection, and audio-alignment workflows require continuous recordings. MultiBlockMaxwell takes raw recording blocks. Source-analysis steps additionally depend on study-specific anatomical and recording information.

Inspect each class's current implementation and tests before building a hardware-specific workflow. A class being available at the top level does not imply that it supports every input representation or has no external requirements.

items.title: Explore full workflows
items.text:
The repository's template pipelines provide examples of more extensive workflows. Treat them as study-dependent starting points rather than universal defaults.

For details on individual processing steps, see the API reference. More specialized workflows are covered in the guides on eye-tracking alignment, audio alignment, and creating custom steps when you need an operation not included here.

items.title: Declare the relationship between steps
items.text:
Each step can define must_be_before, must_be_after, and allow_repeated. Ordering constraints refer to class names as strings, not object labels.

A constraint is checked when the referenced step occurs in the same pipeline. It does not require that step to be present. This allows partial workflows to start from previously processed data.

Declaration Meaning must_be_before = ("SourceReconstruction",) When source reconstruction is present, a matching step must occur later must_be_after = ("Epochs",) When epoch creation is present, a matching step must occur earlier allow_repeated = False Reject more than one instance of the same step type

The current ordering check requires a matching occurrence on the requested side. It is not an all-pairs validator for pipelines containing repeated step types.

items.title: Inspect a concrete rejection
items.text:
Resample declares that an Epochs step, when present, should precede it. This example demonstrates constructor validation and does not need recording data:

from almkanal import AlmKanal, Epochs, Resample

try:
    AlmKanal([
        Resample(sfreq=200),
        Epochs(),
    ])
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)

The proposed order is rejected while building the pipeline. Reordering alone does not supply events or solve all input requirements: the corrected workflow still needs appropriate data and configuration.

Similarly, Maxwell declares that it must precede ICA, ForwardModel, SpatialFilter, and SourceReconstruction when those steps are present.

items.title: Separate ordering checks from data checks
items.text: Constructing AlmKanal(...) checks declared sequence and repetition rules. During execution, individual steps may check data-specific requirements. For example, Resample compares the input's recorded low-pass frequency with half the requested sampling rate and rejects an incompatible downsampling request.

items.title: Add rules to your own step
items.text:
from attrs import define, field
from almkanal import AlmKanalStep

@define
class MySensorStep(AlmKanalStep):
    must_be_before: tuple[str, ...] = field(
        default=("SourceReconstruction",), init=False
    )
    allow_repeated: bool = field(default=False, init=False)

    # Implement run() and reports() before using this step.

This is a declaration example, not a complete processing step. See the custom-step tutorial for a complete implementation.

Scope of the checks. Valid ordering does not guarantee methodological appropriateness, sufficient metadata, compatible hardware, or a successful run. Keep acquisition-specific and scientific checks in your workflow.

items.title: AlmKanalStep
items.text:
AlmKanalStep is the base class for custom preprocessing steps. Subclasses implement run(data, info) to process the data and reports(data, report, info) to update the MNE report.

The run method must return a dictionary containing a data key. Other entries can be used to record information about the processing step. The must_be_before, must_be_after, and allow_repeated attributes control the supported ordering and repetition checks.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal.AlmKanalStep
items.text: This is the base class for all almkanal steps.

items.title: run(data, info)
items.text:
Apply the processing step to the given data.

Child classes must implement this method.

items.title: reports(data, report, info)
items.text:
Update the provided mne.Report object based on the current data.

Child classes must implement this method, and are forced to add something to the report using mne.Report's methods (e.g., add_raw or add_epochs).

items.title: AlmKanal
items.text:
AlmKanal combines an ordered list of preprocessing steps into a pipeline. It checks the supported ordering constraints when the pipeline is created and runs the steps on MNE-Python data.

Create a pipeline with AlmKanal(steps=[...]), then pass the data to pipeline.run(data). The method returns the processed data and an MNE report.

items.title: Artifact and physiological signal processing
items.text: Independent component analysis for artifact correction and processing of physiological signals.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.ica_utils.ICA
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Identify and optionally remove artifacts using independent component analysis.

ICA fits an independent component analysis model to continuous raw data and identifies components associated with physiological or environmental artifacts. Supported artifact classes include eye movements (EOG), cardiac activity (ECG), muscle activity (EMG), and the approximately 16 Hz train-related artifact encountered in recordings acquired in Salzburg.

The data used to fit ICA can be filtered and resampled independently of the original recording. Identified components can either be removed immediately or retained for inspection by setting fit_only=True.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fit_only bool

If True, fit ICA and identify artifact-related components without removing them from the data. If False, identified components are excluded and ICA is applied to the original recording.

False n_components int | float | None

Number of ICA components to estimate. The interpretation follows :class:mne.preprocessing.ICA: an integer specifies an explicit number of components, while a float specifies the fraction of explained variance.

None method str

ICA fitting method passed to :class:mne.preprocessing.ICA.

'picard' random_state int | None

Random seed used during ICA fitting.

None fit_params dict | None

Additional method-specific parameters passed to the ICA fitting procedure.

None ica_hp_freq float | None

High-pass cutoff frequency, in Hz, applied to the copy of the data used for ICA fitting. None disables high-pass filtering.

1.0 ica_lp_freq float | None

Low-pass cutoff frequency, in Hz, applied to the copy of the data used for ICA fitting. None disables low-pass filtering.

None resample_freq int

Sampling frequency, in Hz, used for the data on which ICA is fitted.

200 eog bool

Whether to identify components associated with ocular artifacts.

True surrogate_eog_chs dict | None

Definition of surrogate EOG channels used when dedicated EOG channels are unavailable.

None eog_corr_thresh float

Correlation threshold used to classify components as EOG-related.

0.4 ecg bool

Whether to identify components associated with cardiac artifacts.

True ecg_corr_thresh float

Correlation threshold used to classify components as ECG-related.

0.4 emg bool

Whether to identify components associated with muscle activity.

False emg_thresh float

Threshold used to classify components as EMG-related.

0.5 train bool

Whether to identify components associated with the train-related artifact.

False train_freq float

Frequency, in Hz, around which the train-related artifact is detected.

16.666 train_thresh float

Threshold used to classify components as train-related.

3.0 img_path str | None

Optional image-output path retained as part of the ICA step configuration.

None fname str | None

Optional filename retained as part of the ICA step configuration.

None Notes

ICA preprocessing is performed on a working copy of the recording. Filtering and resampling controlled by ica_hp_freq, ica_lp_freq, and resample_freq therefore do not replace the corresponding preprocessing of the pipeline data itself.

When fit_only=False, components identified as artifacts are excluded and the fitted ICA solution is applied to the original data. When fit_only=True, the fitted ICA model and identified components are returned without modifying the input signal through component removal.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'ica_info'. It contains the fitted ICA object, identified components grouped by artifact type, the applied exclusion list, EOG and ECG scores, and the effective ICA configuration.

Multiple ICA steps are permitted in a pipeline. Reporting uses the most recent occurrence.

See Also

run_ica Fit ICA, identify artifact-related components, and optionally apply the resulting exclusions. mne.preprocessing.ICA MNE-Python implementation of independent component analysis.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.bio_utils.PhysioCleaner
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Preprocess physiological signals in a continuous MNE recording.

PhysioCleaner extracts selected ECG, respiratory, EOG, and EMG channels from a continuous recording and preprocesses them using :func:run_bio_preproc. The resulting data contain the cleaned physiological signals together with stimulus channels retained from the original recording.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ecg str | list | None

ECG channel or channels to preprocess. None disables ECG preprocessing.

None resp str | list | None

Respiratory channel or channels to preprocess. None disables respiratory preprocessing.

None eog str | list | None

EOG channel or channels to preprocess. None disables EOG preprocessing.

None emg str | list | None

EMG channel or channels to preprocess. None disables EMG preprocessing.

None Notes

Physiological preprocessing is delegated to :func:run_bio_preproc, which uses NeuroKit2 to process the selected signals.

The processed recording returned by :meth:run is stored under 'data'. It contains the physiological outputs produced by the preprocessing routine together with the stimulus channels retained from the original recording.

Processing metadata are stored under 'physio_info'. The current metadata include the sampling frequency and signal-specific preprocessing information for ECG, EOG, and EMG processing.

PhysioCleaner can occur only once in a pipeline and is intended to run before forward modelling, spatial filtering, and source reconstruction.

The step currently does not add content to the MNE report.

See Also

run_bio_preproc Preprocess the selected physiological channels.

items.title: Channel cleaning and referencing
items.text: Detection and interpolation of bad EEG channels and re-referencing of electrophysiological data.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.channel_utils.EEGRANSAC
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Detect and interpolate bad EEG channels using RANSAC.

EEGRANSAC uses :class:autoreject.Ransac to identify EEG channels whose signals are poorly predicted from other EEG sensors. Continuous data are first split into fixed-length epochs for RANSAC fitting. Channels identified as bad are then marked in the original recording and interpolated using MNE.

Only EEG channels participate in RANSAC detection and interpolation. Existing bad channels of other channel types are preserved and excluded from the interpolation step.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ransac_epoch_duration int | float

Duration, in seconds, of the fixed-length epochs created from the continuous recording for RANSAC fitting.

4 n_resample int

Number of random sensor subsets used by RANSAC to estimate channel predictability.

50 min_channels float

Fraction of available EEG channels used for robust reconstruction during each RANSAC resampling iteration.

0.25 min_corr float

Minimum correlation between the measured and RANSAC-predicted signal for a channel to be considered sufficiently predictable.

0.75 unbroken_time float

Fraction of time for which a channel may fall below min_corr before it is classified as bad.

0.4 n_jobs int

Number of parallel jobs used by :class:autoreject.Ransac.

1 verbose bool

Whether RANSAC should emit progress and diagnostic output.

False Notes

The continuous recording is segmented into fixed-length epochs solely for RANSAC fitting. These temporary epochs are not returned and do not replace the continuous pipeline data.

Only EEG channels are retained in the temporary RANSAC epochs. ECG, EOG, MEG, and other channel types therefore do not contribute to the bad-channel detection procedure.

Previously marked bad channels are preserved when the newly detected EEG bad channels are added. During interpolation, previously bad non-EEG channels are explicitly excluded so that this step only repairs EEG channels.

Interpolation is performed on the supplied raw object using :meth:mne.io.Raw.interpolate_bads.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'ransac_info' and contains the RANSAC epoch duration and effective RANSAC configuration.

EEGRANSAC may occur multiple times in a pipeline and is intended to run before ICA, forward modelling, spatial filtering, and source reconstruction.

See Also

autoreject.Ransac RANSAC implementation used for bad-channel detection. mne.make_fixed_length_epochs Create the temporary epochs used for RANSAC fitting. mne.io.Raw.interpolate_bads Interpolate channels marked as bad.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.channel_utils.ReReference
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Re-reference EEG, ECoG, sEEG, or DBS channels.

ReReference changes the reference of electrophysiological channels using :meth:mne.io.Raw.set_eeg_reference. It supports references based on one or more existing channels, average referencing, REST referencing, and explicit per-channel reference mappings.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ref_channels str | list of str | dict

Reference specification passed to :meth:mne.io.Raw.set_eeg_reference.

Supported forms include:

  • 'average' to use the average of the selected channel type.
  • 'REST' to apply the Reference Electrode Standardization Technique.
  • A channel name or list of channel names defining the reference.
  • A dictionary mapping data-channel names to one or more reference channels, allowing different references for individual channels.
  • An empty list to leave the data unchanged.
'average' projection bool

Whether an average reference should be added as a projection rather than applied directly to the data. When True with ref_channels='average', the projection is added but is not immediately applied. Other reference schemes require direct re-referencing.

False ch_type str | list of str

Channel type or types to re-reference. Supported types include 'eeg', 'ecog', 'seeg', and 'dbs'. With 'auto', MNE selects the first supported channel type present in the recording.

'auto' forward Forward | None

Forward solution used for REST referencing. Only relevant when ref_channels='REST'.

None joint bool

Whether multiple channel types specified by ch_type should share a common reference. If False, referencing is handled separately for each channel type.

False verbose bool | str | int | None

Verbosity setting passed to :meth:mne.io.Raw.set_eeg_reference.

False Notes

Re-referencing is performed in place on the supplied raw object. The modified object is returned under 'data'.

Except when adding an average-reference projection, the data must be preloaded before the reference can be applied.

For average referencing, channels marked as bad in data.info['bads'] are excluded from the reference calculation by MNE.

REST referencing requires a suitable forward solution supplied through forward.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'ref_info' and contains the reference channels, projection setting, channel types, forward solution, joint-reference setting, and verbosity configuration.

ReReference may occur multiple times in a pipeline and is intended to run before forward modelling, spatial filtering, and source reconstruction.

See Also

mne.io.Raw.set_eeg_reference Change the reference of channels in a raw recording. mne.set_eeg_reference General MNE function for re-referencing Raw, Epochs, or Evoked data.

items.title: Events and epoching
items.text: Extract events from continuous recordings and segment data into epochs.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.event_utils.Events
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Extract discrete events from a continuous raw recording.

Events detects events from one or more stimulus channels using :func:mne.find_events. The detected event array is returned unchanged alongside the original raw object and is stored in the processing history for use by later steps such as Epochs.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default stim_channel str | None

Name of the stimulus channel used for event detection. If None, MNE's default stimulus-channel selection is used.

None output str

Event representation returned by :func:mne.find_events, for example 'onset', 'offset', or 'step'.

'onset' consecutive bool | str

How consecutive non-zero values on the stimulus channel are treated. Passed directly to :func:mne.find_events.

'increasing' min_duration float

Minimum event duration, in seconds.

0.0 shortest_event int

Minimum number of samples that an event must span.

2 mask int | None

Optional bit mask applied to the stimulus channel during event detection.

None uint_cast bool

Whether the stimulus channel should be cast to an unsigned integer representation before event detection.

False mask_type str

Masking operation applied when mask is provided.

'and' initial_event bool

Whether a non-zero stimulus value at the beginning of the recording should be emitted as an event.

False verbose bool | str | int | None

Verbosity setting passed to :func:mne.find_events.

None Notes

Event detection does not modify the input raw data.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'event_info' and contains both the detected events array and the effective event-detection settings.

The resulting event array has the standard MNE shape (n_events, 3) and can be consumed by later processing steps such as Epochs.

Events can occur only once in a pipeline.

See Also

mne.find_events Detect events from stimulus channels. Epochs Create epochs from explicitly supplied or previously detected events.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.epoch_utils.Epochs
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Create epochs from continuous M/EEG data.

Epochs segments a continuous :class:mne.io.BaseRaw recording into time-locked trials using :class:mne.Epochs.

Events can either be supplied directly through events or obtained from the most recent preceding Events step in the processing history. Explicitly supplied events take precedence.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default tmin float

Start of each epoch relative to the event, in seconds.

0. tmax float

End of each epoch relative to the event, in seconds.

0.5 events array - like | None

Event array used to construct the epochs. Expected to follow MNE's standard (n_events, 3) event representation. If None, events are retrieved from the most recent preceding Events step.

None event_id dict | None

Mapping from event names to integer event codes. Passed to :class:mne.Epochs.

None baseline tuple | None

Baseline correction interval in seconds. None disables baseline correction.

None preload bool

Whether to preload epoched data into memory.

True picks str | array - like | None

Channels to include in the epochs.

None reject dict | None

Peak-to-peak amplitude rejection thresholds by channel type.

None flat dict | None

Minimum acceptable peak-to-peak amplitudes by channel type.

None proj bool | str

Projection handling passed to :class:mne.Epochs.

True reject_tmin float | None

Start of the time interval used for rejection, in seconds relative to the event.

None reject_tmax float | None

End of the time interval used for rejection, in seconds relative to the event.

None detrend int | None

Detrending order. 0 removes the mean, 1 removes a linear trend, and None disables detrending.

None on_missing str

Behaviour when entries in event_id are not present in the event array. Passed directly to :class:mne.Epochs.

'raise' reject_by_annotation bool

Whether epochs overlapping annotations marked as bad should be rejected.

True metadata DataFrame | None

Metadata associated with individual epochs.

None event_repeated str

Behaviour when multiple events occur at the same sample. Passed directly to :class:mne.Epochs.

'error' verbose bool | str | int | None

Verbosity setting passed to :class:mne.Epochs.

None Notes

If events is provided directly, no preceding Events step is required. Otherwise, the event array is obtained from the most recent Events entry in the processing history.

The input raw object is not replaced by this step. :meth:run returns a new :class:mne.Epochs object under 'data'.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'epochs_info' and contains the event array together with the effective epoch construction, baseline, channel-selection, rejection, detrending, and metadata settings.

Epochs can occur only once in a pipeline and is expected to run after artifact-correction steps such as Maxwell and ICA and before source modelling and reconstruction steps.

See Also

mne.Epochs MNE-Python class used to construct the epoched data. Events Detect events from a continuous recording for use by this step.

See the eye-tracking guide for recording-specific considerations.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.eye_utils.VPixxCleaner

Load, clean, and align VPixx eye tracking with continuous M/EEG data.
