items.title: Filtering and resampling
items.text: Temporal filtering and changes in sampling frequency for continuous or epoched M/EEG data.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.filter_utils.Filter
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Apply temporal filtering to continuous or epoched M/EEG data.

Filter applies high-pass, low-pass, band-pass, or band-stop filtering using MNE's filtering implementation. The configured filter is applied directly to the supplied :class:mne.io.BaseRaw or :class:mne.BaseEpochs object.

In addition to performing the filter operation, the step records the effective filter settings in the processing history. When transition bandwidths are set to 'auto', concrete values are resolved before filtering so that the reported preprocessing parameters remain explicit and reproducible.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default highpass float | None

High-pass cutoff frequency, in Hz. Passed to MNE as l_freq. None disables high-pass filtering.

None lowpass float | None

Low-pass cutoff frequency, in Hz. Passed to MNE as h_freq. None disables low-pass filtering.

None picks str | array - like | slice | None

Channels to filter. Passed directly to MNE.

None filter_length str | int

Filter length passed to MNE.

'auto' l_trans_bandwidth float | {'auto'}

Transition bandwidth, in Hz, below the high-pass cutoff. When set to 'auto', a concrete value following MNE's default rule is computed before filtering and stored in the processing metadata.

'auto' h_trans_bandwidth float | {'auto'}

Transition bandwidth, in Hz, above the low-pass cutoff. When set to 'auto', a concrete value following MNE's default rule is computed before filtering and stored in the processing metadata.

'auto' n_jobs int | str | None

Number of parallel jobs used for filtering.

None method str

Filtering method passed to MNE, for example 'fir' or 'iir'.

'fir' iir_params dict | None

Parameters used for IIR filtering. When method='iir' and iir_params is None, MNE's effective default Butterworth configuration is recorded in the processing metadata.

None phase str

Phase response used for filtering.

'zero' fir_window str

Window used for FIR filter design.

'hamming' fir_design str

FIR design method passed to MNE.

'firwin' skip_by_annotation str | tuple of str | list of str

Annotation descriptions over which filtering is skipped.

('edge', 'bad_acq_skip') pad str

Padding mode used at the signal boundaries.

'reflect_limited' Notes

The filter is applied in place to the supplied MNE object.

highpass and lowpass correspond to MNE's l_freq and h_freq parameters, respectively. Supplying only highpass produces a high-pass filter, supplying only lowpass produces a low-pass filter, and supplying both produces a band-pass filter.

When transition bandwidths are set to 'auto', the values used for filtering are resolved explicitly before the MNE call. This ensures that the processing history records concrete transition bandwidths rather than the symbolic 'auto' setting.

skip_by_annotation is normalized to a JSON-friendly representation before being stored in the processing metadata.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'filter_info' and contains the effective cutoff frequencies, transition bandwidths, filter design parameters, channel selection, and annotation-skipping configuration.

Filter may occur multiple times in a pipeline.

See Also

mne.io.Raw.filter Filter continuous M/EEG data. mne.Epochs.filter Filter epoched M/EEG data.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.filter_utils.Resample
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Resample continuous or epoched M/EEG data.

Resample changes the sampling frequency of an :class:mne.io.BaseRaw or :class:mne.BaseEpochs object using MNE's resampling implementation.

When downsampling, the step requires the data to have been explicitly low-pass filtered at or below the Nyquist frequency of the requested sampling rate. Although MNE applies anti-aliasing internally during resampling, AlmKanal requires an explicit preceding low-pass filter so that the effective preprocessing settings are recorded in the processing history and can be reported reproducibly.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sfreq int

Target sampling frequency, in Hz.

required npad str

Amount of padding used during resampling. Passed directly to MNE's resample method.

'auto' window str

Window specification used for resampling. Passed directly to MNE's resample method.

'auto' n_jobs int | None

Number of parallel jobs used during resampling.

None pad str

Padding mode used at the signal boundaries.

'auto' method str

Resampling method passed to MNE.

'fft' Notes

Before resampling, the current low-pass frequency is compared with the Nyquist frequency of sfreq. If the low-pass cutoff exceeds the new Nyquist frequency, :meth:run raises a :class:ValueError and instructs the user to apply an explicit anti-aliasing filter first.

Resampling is performed in place on the supplied MNE object.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'resample_info' and contains the target sampling frequency together with the effective resampling parameters.

Resample may occur multiple times in a pipeline.

See Also

mne.io.Raw.resample Resample continuous data. mne.Epochs.resample Resample epoched data.

items.title: Maxwell filtering
items.text: Maxwell filtering for a single continuous MEG recording or for multiple recording blocks.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.channel_utils.Maxwell
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Apply Maxwell filtering to a continuous raw MEG recording.

Maxwell applies Signal Space Separation (SSS) and, optionally, temporal Signal Space Separation (tSSS) to a single :class:mne.io.BaseRaw recording.

The step can also transform the data to a specified destination head position and use system-specific fine-calibration and cross-talk compensation files.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mw_coord_frame str

Coordinate frame used for Maxwell filtering. Typically 'head' or 'meg'.

'head' mw_destination array - like | None

Destination head position used during Maxwell filtering. None keeps the destination behavior defined by the underlying Maxwell-filtering routine.

None mw_st_duration float | None

Temporal Signal Space Separation (tSSS) buffer duration, in seconds. None disables temporal SSS.

None mw_calibration_file str | bool | None

Fine-calibration information passed to Maxwell filtering. A path specifies an external calibration file. With None, calibration embedded in data.info is used when available. True requires embedded calibration information, whereas False disables fine calibration.

None mw_cross_talk_file str | bool | None

Cross-talk compensation passed to Maxwell filtering. A path specifies an external cross-talk file. With None, cross-talk information embedded in data.info is used when available. True requires embedded cross-talk information, whereas False disables it.

None mw_st_correlation float

Correlation threshold used by temporal Signal Space Separation (tSSS). Only relevant when mw_st_duration is not None.

0.98 Notes

The input must be a continuous :class:mne.io.BaseRaw object. Maxwell filtering is performed through :func:run_maxwell using the configured coordinate frame, destination, calibration file, cross-talk file, and tSSS settings.

The processed raw object is returned under 'data'.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'maxwell_info' and contains the effective coordinate frame, destination, calibration file, cross-talk file, and tSSS duration.

Maxwell can occur only once in a pipeline and is intended to run before ICA, forward modelling, spatial filtering, and source reconstruction.

See Also

run_maxwell Apply Maxwell filtering to a raw MEG recording. MultiBlockMaxwell Apply Maxwell filtering to multiple recording blocks before concatenating them.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.channel_utils.MultiBlockMaxwell
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Apply Maxwell filtering to multiple raw MEG recording blocks.

MultiBlockMaxwell applies Maxwell filtering independently to each raw MEG block and then concatenates the filtered blocks into a single continuous recording.

All blocks are transformed to a common destination position before concatenation. If mw_destination is not provided, the destination is computed from the median device-to-head translation across all input blocks.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mw_coord_frame str

Coordinate frame used for Maxwell filtering. Typically 'head' or 'meg'.

'head' mw_destination array - like | None

Destination head position used during Maxwell filtering. If None, a common destination is derived by taking the median of the translation components of info['dev_head_t'] across all input blocks.

None mw_calibration_file str | None

Path to the fine-calibration file used by Maxwell filtering.

None mw_cross_talk_file str | None

Path to the cross-talk compensation file used by Maxwell filtering.

None mw_st_duration float | None

Temporal Signal Space Separation (tSSS) buffer duration, in seconds. None disables temporal SSS.

None mw_st_correlation float

Correlation threshold used by temporal Signal Space Separation (tSSS) for each recording block. Only relevant when mw_st_duration is not None.

0.98 Notes

The input to :meth:run must be a list of :class:mne.io.BaseRaw objects. Each block is Maxwell filtered separately using the same coordinate frame, destination, calibration file, cross-talk file, and tSSS configuration.

When mw_destination is None, the common destination is computed from the median three-dimensional translation of the device-to-head transforms across all blocks. This provides a shared head position to which all blocks are aligned before concatenation.

After Maxwell filtering, the processed blocks are concatenated with :func:mne.concatenate_raws and returned as a single continuous raw object.

The processing metadata returned by :meth:run is stored under 'maxwell_info' and contains the effective coordinate frame, destination, calibration file, cross-talk file, and tSSS duration.

MultiBlockMaxwell can occur only once in a pipeline and is intended to run before ICA, forward modelling, spatial filtering, and source reconstruction.

See Also

run_maxwell Apply Maxwell filtering to an individual raw recording. mne.concatenate_raws Concatenate the filtered raw blocks.

items.title: Source modelling and reconstruction
items.text: Build forward models and reconstruct source activity from sensor-space recordings.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.headmodel_utils.ForwardModel
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Build an MEG forward model for source reconstruction.

The forward model combines the sensor geometry, MEG-to-MRI coregistration, source space, and boundary-element model (BEM).

Individual FreeSurfer reconstructions are expected under subjects_dir / 'freesurfer' / subject_id. When template anatomy is used, fsaverage is scaled to the participant and stored as <subject_id>_from_template.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default subject_id str

Subject identifier.

required subjects_dir str | Path

AlmKanal working directory. FreeSurfer subjects are stored under subjects_dir / 'freesurfer' and coregistration outputs under subjects_dir / 'headmodels'.

required pick_dict dict | None

Channel selection passed to :func:mne.pick_types before coregistration. If None, channel picks are taken from the pipeline information when available.

required source (surface, volume)

Type of source space used for the forward model. Default is 'surface'.

'surface' redo_hdm bool

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.spatial_filter_utils.SpatialFilter
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Compute LCMV spatial filters for source reconstruction.

SpatialFilter computes data and noise covariance matrices as needed and constructs an LCMV beamformer for subsequent source reconstruction. The forward model and channel-selection parameters can either be supplied directly or obtained from preceding pipeline configuration.

If an empty-room recording is used to estimate the noise covariance, the relevant preprocessing history is passed along so that compatible preprocessing can be applied to the empty-room data before covariance estimation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fwd Forward | None

Forward model used to construct the spatial filter. If None, the forward solution produced by a preceding ForwardModel step is used.

None pick_dict dict | None

Channel-selection parameters used for spatial filtering. If None, the pipeline-level pick_params stored in :class:AlmKanalInfo are used. A value must be available from one of these sources.

None data_cov Covariance | None

Precomputed data covariance matrix. If None, it is computed from the input data.

None noise_cov Covariance | None

Precomputed noise covariance matrix. If provided, it is used directly. Otherwise, a covariance can be derived from empty_room or, when no empty-room data are supplied, according to the fallback behaviour of :func:comp_spatial_filters.

None empty_room str | BaseRaw | None

Empty-room recording used to estimate the noise covariance. May be a path to a recording or an already loaded :class:mne.io.BaseRaw instance.

None nearest_empty_room bool

Whether an empty-room recording nearest in acquisition date should be selected when resolving empty-room data.

False chans2keep list of str | None

Channels to preserve separately before spatial-filter channel selection, for example stimulus features, ECG, EOG, or eye-tracking channels. Their data are stored in the returned spatial-filter metadata.

None lcmv_reg float

Regularization parameter passed to the LCMV beamformer computation.

0.05 lcmv_pick_ori str | None

Source-orientation selection passed to the LCMV beamformer.

'max-power' lcmv_weight_norm str | None

Weight-normalization method passed to the LCMV beamformer.

'nai' lcmv_reduce_rank bool

Whether to reduce the rank during LCMV filter construction.

False Notes

pick_dict takes precedence over pipeline-level pick_params. If neither is available, :meth:run raises a :class:ValueError.

Likewise, an explicitly supplied fwd takes precedence over the forward model stored by a preceding ForwardModel step.

The input data are returned unchanged. Computed spatial-filter information is stored under 'spatial_filter_info' and contains the beamformer filters, effective LCMV settings, data covariance, noise covariance, and any channels preserved through chans2keep.

When empty-room data are used, the pipeline's ordered processing history is passed to the empty-room preprocessing machinery so that relevant previous preprocessing steps can be replayed before estimating the noise covariance.

SpatialFilter is intended to precede SourceReconstruction and can occur only once in a pipeline.

See Also

items.title: Stimulus epoching and WAV alignment
items.text:
StimulusEpochs divides each stimulus trial into non-overlapping, fixed-length epochs and appends one or more WAV-derived stimulus features. The resulting epochs can be used for TRFs and other analyses. Use feature="envelope" for a single feature or feature=["envelope", "mel_onsets"] to append several features. resample_sfreq=200.0 resamples trial segments after alignment and physical-delay correction, before computing features at 200 Hz; None retains the input rate.

StimulusSpanSpec describes the trial spans and audio files used for this workflow.

StimulusSpanSpec is a supporting data class, not an AlmKanalStep. See the WAV-alignment guide for workflow details.

items.title: almkanal.almkanal_steps.stimulus_utils.StimulusEpochs
items.text:
Bases: AlmKanalStep

Create fixed-length epochs within stimulus trials and attach WAV features.

Optionally correct the recording clock, apply a fixed neural timing shift, then split trials into non-overlapping epochs with WAV features as misc channels. Defaults below describe the general profile; omitted settings use the active profile captured when the step is constructed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default gen_span_spec callable

Callback gen_span_spec(raw) -> StimulusSpanSpec supplying trial spans, WAV paths, and optional metadata for the input recording.

required base_audio_path str | Path

Directory used to resolve relative WAV paths in the generated span spec.

required resample_sfreq float | None

Output sampling frequency in Hz. Resample continuous trial segments after alignment and physical-delay correction, before extracting and appending features. None retains the input rate. Uses FFT resampling with a boxcar window, automatic padding, and reflect_limited edge padding; MNE applies anti-aliasing internally. Trial spans always refer to input samples.

None feature str | sequence of str

One or more distinct WAV features, appended in the requested order. Single-channel features use the requested name; multichannel features use that name as a prefix followed by component or band identifiers. Names must not overlap existing recording channels. Available features: 'envelope' (RMS), 'rectify', 'mel', 'flux', 'mel_onsets', 'pitch', or 'pitch_voicing'. See prepare_audio.

'envelope' audio_cutoff_hz float

Low-pass cutoff in Hz for WAV features, capped below their Nyquist rate.

80.0 hw_delay_s float

Neural timing shift in seconds, applied after clock correction. Positive values advance neural events; negative values add lag and warn.

0.0 epoch_len_s float

Duration of each non-overlapping epoch in seconds. Must be positive; incomplete trailing epochs are discarded.

5.0 audio_channels sequence of str | None

Recorded audio channel names for estimating offset and drift. None disables measured alignment; see realign_without_audio.

None alignment_kwargs mapping | None

Overrides for estimate_raw_wav_alignment, e.g. {'max_lag_s': 1.0}. Requires audio_channels; None uses the captured alignment defaults.

None preserve_annotations bool

Keep annotations and reject epochs overlapping bad intervals. False removes annotations before epoching.

True on_alignment_error ('raise', 'skip')

Raise on alignment failure, or warn, record the failure, and skip the trial. Applies to measured and assumed alignment, not quality warnings.

'raise' verbose bool

Emit processing messages. Quality warnings are shown regardless.

True realign_without_audio bool

Resample using assumed drift and WAV duration when audio_channels is None. Assumes WAV time zero at the trial onset.

False fallback_drift_us_per_s float

Assumed drift in microseconds per second for realign_without_audio and, by default, missing-end inference in gen_span_spec.

0.0 must_be_before tuple of str

Step class names that must follow this step if present in the pipeline.

() must_be_after tuple of str

Step class names that must precede this step if present in the pipeline.

() Notes
  • Recorded audio: takes precedence over assumed drift and needs sufficient signal bandwidth. Failed fits follow on_alignment_error without falling back to assumed drift. For long stimuli, increase alignment_kwargs['max_lag_s'] to cover offset plus accumulated drift; see estimate_raw_wav_alignment for search limits and quality warnings.
  • Assumed drift: uses t_raw = (1 + drift / 1e6) * t_wav relative to trial onset. Positive drift lengthens raw time. The WAV determines trial duration; the end trigger does not determine drift. No offset is measured.
  • Physical delay: applied after clock correction, rounded to a sample. WAV features stay unchanged. Use zero if the audio reference already represents sound arrival at the ears. Alignment needs raw coverage for the full WAV plus delay margins; insufficient coverage is an alignment error.
  • Salzburg defaults: hw_delay_s=0.0165 compensates the 16.5 ms air-tube delay when the reference precedes the tubes. The profile also sets audio_channels=('MISC007', 'MISC008') and fallback_drift_us_per_s=499.0. Pass audio_channels=None explicitly to use assumed drift with this profile.
See Also

StimulusSpanSpec : Trial spans, WAV paths, and optional metadata. build_stimulus_epochs : Standalone epoch builder using an existing span spec. estimate_raw_wav_alignment : Alignment options and fit diagnostics. prepare_audio : Available WAV features and their output channels.

items.text:
Build fixed-length stimulus epochs with stimulus features from WAV files.

Defaults below describe the general profile; omitted configurable settings use the active defaults profile.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default raw BaseRaw

Continuous recording to epoch. The input is not modified.

required spec StimulusSpanSpec

Trial spans, WAV paths, and optional per-trial metadata.

required base_audio_path str | Path

Directory used to resolve relative WAV paths in spec.

required resample_sfreq float | None

Output sampling frequency in Hz. Resample continuous trial segments after alignment and physical-delay correction, before extracting and appending features. None retains the input rate. Uses FFT resampling with a boxcar window, automatic padding, and reflect_limited edge padding; MNE applies anti-aliasing internally. Trial spans always refer to input samples.

None feature str | sequence of str

One or more distinct WAV features, appended in the requested order. Single-channel features use the requested name; multichannel features use that name as a prefix followed by component or band identifiers. Names must not overlap existing recording channels. Available features: 'envelope' (RMS), 'rectify', 'mel', 'flux', 'mel_onsets', 'pitch', or 'pitch_voicing'. See prepare_audio.

'envelope' audio_cutoff_hz float

Low-pass cutoff in Hz for WAV features, capped below their Nyquist rate.

80.0 hw_delay_s float

Neural timing shift in seconds, applied after clock correction. Positive values advance neural events; negative values add lag and warn.

0.0 epoch_len_s float

Duration of each non-overlapping epoch in seconds. Must be positive; incomplete trailing epochs are discarded.

5.0 wav_ext str

Suffix used to turn labels without a wav_by_label entry into paths.

'.wav' audio_channels sequence of str | None

Recorded audio channel names for estimating offset and drift. None disables measured alignment; see realign_without_audio.

None realign_without_audio bool

Resample using assumed drift and WAV duration when audio_channels is None. Assumes WAV time zero at the trial onset.

False fallback_drift_us_per_s float

Assumed drift in microseconds per second for realign_without_audio. Positive values mean the recording clock spans more time than the WAV.

0.0 alignment_kwargs mapping | None

Overrides for estimate_raw_wav_alignment, e.g. {'max_lag_s': 1.0}. Requires audio_channels; None uses the active alignment defaults.

None preserve_annotations bool

Keep annotations and reject epochs overlapping bad intervals. False removes annotations before epoching.

True on_alignment_error ('raise', 'skip')

Raise on alignment failure, or warn and skip the affected trial. Applies to measured and assumed alignment, not fit-quality warnings.

'raise' verbose bool

Emit processing messages. Quality warnings are shown regardless.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description epochs Epochs

Concatenated epochs with the input channels, WAV features as misc channels, and trial/timing metadata. Raises if no epochs survive.

Notes

Recorded audio takes precedence over assumed drift, including when a fit fails. Clock correction precedes the sample-rounded hw_delay_s shift; WAV features are not shifted. Alignment requires recording coverage for the full WAV duration plus any physical-delay margins.

The Salzburg profile uses hw_delay_s=0.0165, audio_channels ('MISC007', 'MISC008'), and fallback_drift_us_per_s=499.0. See :class:StimulusEpochs for delay conventions and assumed-drift behavior.

See Also
